lines: The air changes immediately. No raider graffiti here, no crude modifications — this section of the Spire has been left untouched. Perhaps the Luddites feared what they couldn't understand.
Crystal shelves line the walls, holding objects that might be books, or might be something else entirely. Geometric patterns pulse with faint inner light when you draw near.
Reading pedestals stand at intervals through the archives. Whatever knowledge the Underlumen builders stored here, it has waited patiently for someone to find it.
The pedestal activates at your touch. Light coalesces into geometric patterns — a language of pure structure.
You can't read it, but the meaning seeps through: this Spire was a watchtower in the truest sense. Not watching for enemies, but watching the boundary between the surface world and something deeper.
The builders called themselves Vigil-keepers. They monitored a resonance — a frequency that connects the Underlumen network across vast distances.
Another pedestal hums to life. This one shows schematics — cross-sections of the Spire extending deep underground, far deeper than the raiders have explored.
Below the fortress levels, the Spire descends into what the builders called the Resonance Chamber — a place where the boundary between nodes grows thin.
The schematics show energy pathways converging on a central core. Whatever powers the Underlumen network, this Spire is one of its anchor points.
The third pedestal shows something different — a warning. The geometric patterns pulse red, urgent even after millennia.
The Resonance Chamber was sealed deliberately. Not to keep intruders out, but to keep something contained. The builders detected an anomaly in the network — a frequency that didn't belong.
They couldn't eliminate it. They could only contain it. The Spire of Vigil was built specifically for this purpose: to watch, and to hold.

actions.text: A reflecting pool of perfectly still water fills the central atrium. The crystal ceiling above focuses ambient light into the water, creating patterns that shift like constellations.
